architecture_decisions.recommendation: Replaced in-memory manifest accumulation with streaming writes using StreamingManifestWriter class
architecture_decisions.rationale: The original implementation accumulated all manifest records in memory (manifest_dict) before writing, causing high memory usage for large exports. The streaming approach writes records incrementally to a temporary file, significantly reducing peak memory consumption while maintaining data integrity.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Implemented atomic file operations with temporary files and BLAKE2b hash comparison
architecture_decisions.rationale: The StreamingManifestWriter writes to a .tmp file first, then performs atomic rename only after successful completion. This prevents partial/corrupted manifests and supports the --compare-json option using cryptographically secure BLAKE2b hashes instead of MD5 for integrity verification.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added context manager pattern with proper cleanup on exceptions
architecture_decisions.rationale: The StreamingManifestWriter implements __enter__ and __exit__ methods to ensure temporary files are cleaned up on exceptions while preserving the original manifest file. This maintains system consistency even when exports fail mid-process.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Changed from batch encryption to per-record encryption with O(1) lookup
architecture_decisions.rationale: Previously encrypted all sensitive fields in a batch after manifest accumulation. Now encrypts records inline during streaming using CRYPT_FIELDS_BY_MODEL dictionary for efficient field lookup, enabling encryption to work with the streaming architecture.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added test for folder_prefix with split_manifest combination
architecture_decisions.rationale: The new test ensures the streaming implementation works correctly with the complex interaction between use_folder_prefix and split_manifest options, which create nested directory structures and multiple manifest files.

implementation_summary:
The implementation addresses memory optimization in the document exporter by introducing a streaming architecture that replaces in-memory manifest accumulation. The core change is the StreamingManifestWriter class, which incrementally writes JSON records to a temporary file and performs atomic replacement upon successful completion. This class uses a context manager pattern for robust error handling, ensuring temporary files are cleaned up on exceptions while preserving existing manifests.

Key architectural changes include: 1) Restructuring the export command to process records in batches and write them immediately rather than accumulating everything in memory, 2) Moving encryption from a batch operation to per-record encryption using an optimized lookup dictionary (CRYPT_FIELDS_BY_MODEL), 3) Enhancing file comparison to use BLAKE2b hashes instead of MD5 for better security, and 4) Maintaining backward compatibility with existing options like --split-manifest and --compare-json.

The implementation follows the existing Django management command patterns while introducing a more memory-efficient approach. The streaming writer handles the complexity of JSON array formatting (commas, newlines, brackets) internally, allowing the main export logic to focus on document processing. This change significantly reduces peak memory usage during large exports while maintaining all existing functionality and adding proper atomic file operations for data integrity.
